title: Twist E30: Two-box incidence encoding and a matched ordinary control
status_note: Partial local pilot: all 270 finite-grid cells and independent PARI replay pass; zero degree reductions versus direct membership. Full solver/cost comparison and raw publication remain open. Blocked and unfunded.
blocked_on: note:Complete solver/lifting and cold construction costs for the exact same projected bases are missing.
question: Can a two-box twist incidence encoding lower complete decomposition cost against direct membership and a generic ordinary encoding of the same projected base?
decision_value: A verified same-base complete-cost gain supports an encoding improvement. A lower displayed degree alone does not, and an ordinary-mask match must be priced before attributing any benefit to the twist.

resources.notes: Bounded local correctness pilot: one worker, 4 GiB, native 3600-second and PARI 600-second caps. Full solver/cost and disk estimates remain uncalibrated; no scheduled job or funding.

outputs.result_schema: Partial local twist.followup-run/v1 finite-incidence certificates; full comparison not complete.

env.recipe: Design only; implement native driver, independent checker, checkpoints and source/protocol pins before readiness.

funding.rationale: Blocked proposal with no run estimate, below the existing funded seed cards. Adding it changes no runnable-work priority or funding.
